# Getting Support

This document is the default support policy for repositories owned by
[@carlosferreyra](https://github.com/carlosferreyra) that do not define their
own `SUPPORT.md`.

## Before opening an issue

1. **Read the project's README** and any linked documentation.
2. **Search existing issues** (open and closed) — your question may already be
   answered.
3. **Search GitHub Discussions** if the repository has them enabled.

## Where to get help

| I want to…                        | Go here                                                                           |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ask a usage question              | Use the repository's Discussions tab, when enabled, or open a `question` issue |
| Report a reproducible bug         | Open a [bug report](./ISSUE_TEMPLATE/01-bug_report.yml)                           |
| Request a new feature             | Open a [feature request](./ISSUE_TEMPLATE/02-feature_request.yml)                 |
| Report a security vulnerability   | Follow the [Security Policy](./SECURITY.md) — **do not** open a public issue      |
| Contribute code or docs           | Read the [Contributing Guide](./CONTRIBUTING.md)                                  |
| Contact the maintainer privately  | Email [contact@carlosferreyra.me](mailto:contact@carlosferreyra.me)               |

## Response expectations

These projects are maintained on a best-effort basis. Typical response times:

- **Security reports**: acknowledged within 3 business days.
- **Bug reports & feature requests**: triaged within 7 days.
- **General questions**: no guaranteed SLA — community answers welcome.

## What to include in a support request

- Repository name and version / commit SHA.
- Operating system, runtime, and language versions.
- A minimal reproducible example (code, commands, logs).
- Expected vs. actual behavior.

Clear, minimal reproductions get faster responses.
